issues.body: The workflow has `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true` for each issue. This step reads an absent pre-state, writes `trust:untrusted`, verifies it, and only then posts the notice. If a newer `edited`/`labeled` event cancels the run after the label write but before `gh issue comment` completes, the replacement run reads `trust:untrusted` and skips the comment. All subsequent events do the same, so the issue may never receive even one quarantine notice. The same permanent suppression follows from a first comment attempt that fails, because the label remains the only remembered state. Thus presence of the security label is being used as evidence of a separate side effect that it does not prove. The new self-tests run each shell invocation to completion and cannot detect the cancellation window.
issues.fix_hint: De-duplicate against evidence that the notice itself exists (for example, an exact bot-authored marker/comment check with quoted/untrusted content excluded), while retaining the fail-open direction for this courtesy read so label application cannot be delayed. Add an executable case representing interruption after the verified label write and prove a later event still posts exactly one notice. Alternatively introduce a sound atomic/serialized protocol whose committed marker cannot precede the notice.
issues.title: Cancellation can permanently suppress a notice that was never posted

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The sequential paths are well exercised and preserve the quarantine label write, but the label is not a sound de-duplication marker for the courtesy comment under this workflow's actual cancellation semantics. A run can persist `trust:untrusted` and then be cancelled before commenting; every later run will treat that label as proof that the notice was already posted. The added tests execute the shell only to completion and therefore miss this production seam.
